'''Deni Avdija''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|d|ɛ|n|i|_|ə|v|ˈ|d|iː|j|ə}} {{respell|DEN|ee|_|av|DEE|ya}}; {{langx|he|דֶנִי אָבְדִיָה}}, {{lang-sr-Cyrl|Дени Авдија}}; born 3 January 2001) is an Israeli-Serbian professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He plays the [[small forward]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Deni Avdija Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft Status and more |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/a/avdijde01.html |access-date=2025-11-23 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> position, and is nicknamed "'''Turbo'''" for his fast-paced drive and aggressive playing style.<ref>{{cite web|title= Where Deni Avdija's new nickname Turbo comes from|url= https://wtop.com/washington-wizards/2023/01/where-deni-avdijas-new-nickname-turbo-comes-from/|website= wtop.com}}</ref> Prior to the NBA, he played for [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]] in Israel. From 2020 to 2024, he played for the [[Washington Wizards]]. In 2024, Avdija was traded to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].

The son of former Serbian-Gorani basketball player [[Zufer Avdija]], he started playing basketball in the fourth grade for his hometown club [[Bnei Herzliya Basket]], and then in 2013 for [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]]. He excelled as a youth player. He debuted for their senior team in 2017, at age 16, becoming the youngest player in club history. Two years later, he became the youngest player to ever win the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League MVP]] award, and led his team to the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League]] championship. He deferred his [[Conscription in Israel|mandatory Israel Defense Forces (IDF) service]] until 2020, when NBA games were suspended during the [[COVID-19 pandemic]]. 

In 2020, Avdija declared for the [[2020 NBA draft|NBA draft]] and was drafted by the [[Washington Wizards]] with the 9th overall pick. He is also a member of the [[Israel national basketball team|Israeli senior national basketball team]]. He has won two [[gold medal]]s for Israel at the youth level, including at the [[2019 FIBA U20 European Championship]], where he was named tournament's [[most valuable player]].

==Early life and youth career==
Avdija was born in [[kibbutz]] [[Beit Zera]] in Israel. His mother, Sharon Artzi, an [[Israeli Jews|Israeli Jew]] from the kibbutz, is a former [[track and field]] and basketball player.<ref name="maccabi">{{cite web |title=Deni Avdija |url=http://www.maccabi.co.il/player.asp?PlayerID=955&cYear=2020&lang=en |publisher=[[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]] |access-date=11 April 2020}}</ref> His father, [[Zufer Avdija]], is an Israeli citizen with a [[Muslims|Muslim]]-[[Gorani people|Gorani]] heritage <ref name="maccabi" /><ref name="obsession" /><ref name="griver">{{cite web |last1=Griver |first1=Simon |date=31 March 2020 |title=Avdija tipped to be no. 1 in NBA draft |url=https://www.thejc.com/life/sport/avdija-tipped-to-be-no-1-in-nba-draft-glirddzn |access-date=10 April 2020 |website=[[The Jewish Chronicle]]}}</ref> who played basketball for the [[Yugoslavia men's national basketball team|Yugoslavia national team]] before moving to Israel to play for Israeli teams.<ref name="sachs">{{cite web |last1=Sachs |first1=Frankie |title=Conversation with Deni Avdija, Maccabi |url=https://www.euroleague.net/news/i/a4w8t8pomc8mgpwm/conversation-with-deni-avdija-maccabi |publisher=[[EuroLeague]] |access-date=10 April 2020 |date=23 October 2019}}</ref>

Deni Avdija played [[association football]] until he entered fourth grade, when his friend and teammate Itamar Vule convinced him to try basketball because of his height. He started focusing more on basketball. In 2013, he joined the youth ranks of [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]], where he played under the coach Shai Omer.<ref name=Bio>{{cite web|title=מניה בצמיחה / דני אבדיה הוא הדבר הבא|url=https://www.ynet.co.il/articles/0,7340,L-5311930,00.html|publisher=[[Ynet]]|access-date=21 July 2018|date=18 July 2018|language=he}}</ref> From 2017 to 2019, Avdija led [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]] to three consecutive Israeli youth state championships.<ref>{{Cite web|title=בפעם הרביעית ברציפות: קבוצת הנוער של מכבי ת"א זכתה באליפות|url=https://www.ynet.co.il/articles/0,7340,L-5517407,00.html|publisher= [[Ynet]] |access-date=31 May 2019|date=29 May 2019|language=he}}</ref> In August 2018, he participated in [[Basketball Without Borders]] Europe in [[Belgrade]], where he was named camp MVP.<ref>{{cite web |title=Jokic, Vucevic Headline Basketball Without Borders Europe 2018 |url=http://global.nba.com/news/jokic-vucevic-headline-basketball-without-borders-europe-2018/ |publisher=[[National Basketball Association|NBA]] | date=14 August 2018 |access-date=18 August 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Djordjevic |first1=Stefan |title=Deni Avdija named Basketball Without Borders MVP |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/nba-news/726859/deni-avdija-named-basketball-without-borders-mvp/ |publisher=EuroHoops| date=18 August 2018 | access-date=18 August 2018}}</ref> In December 2018 he led his [[Tichon Hadash]] high school team to win the Israeli championship for high schools.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2018-12-20 |title=הצגה לדני אבדיה, תיכון חדש ת"א אלופת התיכונים |url=https://www.ynet.co.il/articles/0,7340,L-5430138,00.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181220212642/https://www.ynet.co.il/articles/0,7340,L-5430138,00.html |archive-date=2018-12-20 |access-date=2025-10-07 |work=ynet |language=he}}</ref>

Avdija initially competed at the youth level for [[Bnei Herzliya]], and in January 2019, Avdija played for Maccabi Tel Aviv's U18 team at the [[2018–19 Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament|Adidas Next Generation Tournament]] (ANGT) in [[Munich]]. He was selected to the all-tournament team after leading the event with 24.3 [[point (basketball)|points]], 6 [[assist (basketball)|assists]], and 3.8 [[steal (basketball)|steals]] per game and a [[Performance Index Rating]] (PIR) of 31.5. Avdija also ranked second among all players with 11 [[rebound (basketball)|rebounds]] per game, while helping his team finish in second place.<ref name="hein">{{cite web |last1=Hein |first1=David |title=Maccabi's Avdija is just #LivingTheDream |url=https://www.adidasngt.com/u18/news/latest/i/9felb3mwhqcicmyh/maccabi-s-avdija-is-just-livingthedream |publisher=[[Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament]] |access-date=10 April 2020 |date=28 January 2019 |archive-date=10 April 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200410223841/https://www.adidasngt.com/u18/news/latest/i/9felb3mwhqcicmyh/maccabi-s-avdija-is-just-livingthedream |url-status=dead }}</ref> In February 2019, at the [[2019 NBA All-Star Game#All-Star Weekend|NBA All-Star Weekend]] in [[Charlotte, North Carolina]], Avdija was named MVP of the Basketball Without Borders Global Camp.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Gay |first1=Carlan | title=Deni Avdija, Aaliyah Mckenzie Edwards take home MVP at Basketball Without Borders Global 2019 | url=https://ca.nba.com/news/deni-avdija-aaliyah-mckenzie-edwards-mvp-at-bwb-gloabl-2019-recap/oxb4bvwlgnx01o3xb5eakhvtm | website=[[NBA.com]] | access-date=18 February 2019 | date=18 February 2019}}</ref> In May, he joined Maccabi Tel Aviv's U18 team for the [[2018–19 Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament#Final Tournament|ANGT Finals]]. He collected all-tournament team honours after leading the event with 24.7 points and 12 rebounds per game with a PIR of 29.7, while ranking second with 6.7 assists per game.<ref name="angtfinals">{{cite web |title=MVP Nakic of Real Madrid headlines All-Tournament Team |url=https://www.adidasngt.com/u18/news/latest/i/9occvq9c8tn4qe63/mvp-nakic-of-real-madrid-headlines-all-tournament-team |publisher=[[Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament]] |access-date=10 April 2020 |date=19 May 2019}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Maccabi Tel Aviv (2017–2020)===
On 5 November 2017, Avdija started his professional career with Israeli club [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]], signing a six-year deal with the club.<ref>{{Cite web|last1=Carchia|first1=Emiliano|title=Maccabi Tel Aviv signs prospect Deni Avdija to a six-year contract|url=http://archive.sportando.basketball/en/europe/israel/252732/maccabi-tel-aviv-signs-prospect-deni-avdija-to-a-six-year-contract.html|publisher=Sportando|access-date=21 July 2018|date=5 November 2017|archive-date=20 August 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200820105710/http://archive.sportando.basketball/en/europe/israel/252732/maccabi-tel-aviv-signs-prospect-deni-avdija-to-a-six-year-contract.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> On 19 November, he made his professional debut in the [[2017–18 Israeli Basketball Premier League]], playing three minutes against [[Ironi Nes Ziona B.C.|Ironi Nes Ziona]]. At 16 years and 320 days of age, he became the youngest player to ever play for his club's senior team.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Winner League, Game 7: Nes Ziona Vs M. Tel-Aviv|url=http://basket.co.il/game-zone.asp?GameId=23190&lang=en|publisher=[[Israeli Basketball Premier League|Israeli Premier League]]|access-date=21 July 2018|date=19 November 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=חי את החלום – דני אבדיה בראיון|url=http://www.maccabi.co.il/magazines/newsPage.asp?newsID=981|publisher=[[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]]|access-date=2 November 2019|date=7 February 2019|language=he}}</ref> Avdija made his [[EuroLeague]] debut on 22 November 2018, at the age of 17, in a 74–70 loss to [[Fenerbahçe Basketball|Fenerbahçe]]. He scored two points in three minutes of playing time.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=67&seasoncode=E2018#!boxscore|title=Maccabi FOX Tel Aviv vs. Fenerbahce BEKO Istanbul – Game|publisher=[[EuroLeague]]|access-date=12 February 2020|date=22 November 2018}}</ref>

[[File:Deni Avdija Maccabi (cropped) 2.jpg|thumb|left|Avdija with [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]] in 2019]]

On 24 October 2019, at the age of 18, Avdija made his first start in the [[EuroLeague]], recording six points and three rebounds in 16 minutes in a 76–63 victory over [[Valencia Basket|Valencia]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=67&seasoncode=E2018#!boxscore|title=Maccabi FOX Tel Aviv vs. Valencia Basket – Game|publisher=[[EuroLeague]]|access-date=26 October 2019|date=24 October 2019}}</ref> On 11 January 2020, Avdija recorded a then career-high of 22 points, shooting 9-of-15 from the field, with five assists in a 94–83 win over [[Hapoel Holon B.C.|Hapoel Holon]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Winner League, Game 15: U-NET Holon Vs M. Tel-Aviv|url=http://basket.co.il/game-zone.asp?GameId=24109&lang=en|publisher=[[Israeli Basketball Premier League|Israeli Premier League]]|access-date=11 January 2020|date=11 January 2020}}</ref> On 31 January, Avdija was named [[2019–20 Israeli Basketball Premier League#Israeli Player of the Month|Israeli Player of the Month]] in the Israeli Basketball Premier League after averaging 14.5 points, 5.3 rebounds, and 2.5 assists per game, with an 18.3 PIR, in four games played that month.<ref>{{cite news|title=שחקן החודש הישראלי: דני אבדיה|url=http://basket.co.il/news.asp?id=23112|publisher=[[Israeli Basketball Premier League|Israeli Premier League]]|date=31 January 2020|access-date=31 January 2020|language=he}}</ref> On 1 February, Avdija established a new career-high of 26 points, shooting 9-of-12 from the field, and grabbed six rebounds in an 86–81 loss to [[Hapoel Eilat B.C.|Hapoel Eilat]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Winner League, Game 18: Hapoel Yossi Avrahami Eilat Vs M. Tel-Aviv|url=http://basket.co.il/game-zone.asp?GameId=24125&lang=en|publisher=[[Israeli Basketball Premier League|Israeli Premier League]]|date=1 February 2020|access-date=1 February 2020}}</ref> Six days later, he scored 13 points, including eight in the second quarter, in a 78–77 victory over Fenerbahçe.<ref>{{cite web |title=Hunter lifts Maccabi at finish over Fenerbahce |url=https://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=213&seasoncode=E2019#!report |publisher=[[EuroLeague]] |access-date=19 July 2020 |date=7 February 2020}}</ref> His dunk over [[Luigi Datome]] during the game would be named [[EuroLeague Magic Moment of the Season]] in July 2020.<ref>{{Cite tweet |user=EuroLeague |author=EuroLeague |number=1284877355534737408 |date = 19 July 2020 |title=Here it is... The @7DAYSBasketball Magic Moment of the 2019/20 season The Deni Avdija Poster Jam}}</ref> On 16 April, Avdija declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]].<ref name="draft">{{cite web |last1=Givony |first1=Jonathan |title=Potential top-five pick Deni Avdija seeks entry to 2020 NBA draft |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/29043324/potential-top-five-pick-deni-avdija-seeks-entry-2020-nba-draft |publisher=[[ESPN]] |access-date=17 April 2020 |date=16 April 2020}}</ref>

Avdija's season was suspended for about three months due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]]. He returned to action on 21 June, recording 23 points, seven rebounds, and five assists in 24 minutes in a 114–82 win over [[Maccabi Ashdod B.C.|Maccabi Ashdod]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Deni Avdija erupts with 23 points in Israeli League's return |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/others/1072537/deni-avdija-erupts-with-23-points-in-israeli-leagues-return/ |publisher=EuroHoops |access-date=21 June 2020 |date=21 June 2020}}</ref> On 23 July, he scored 22 points, including 10 in the fourth quarter, and grabbed 10 rebounds in an 83–68 win over [[Hapoel Tel Aviv B.C.|Hapoel Tel Aviv]], helping Maccabi Tel Aviv advance to the Israeli Basketball Premier League Final Four.<ref>{{cite web |title=Dorsey, Avdija step up and lift shorthanded Maccabi over Hapoel to win the series |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/others/1083800/dorsey-avdija-step-up-and-lift-shorthanded-maccabi-over-hapoel-to-win-the-series/ |publisher=EuroHoops |access-date=23 July 2020 |date=23 July 2020}}</ref> In the Final on 28 July, Avdija recorded five points, seven rebounds, four assists, and two steals to help Maccabi Tel Aviv defeat [[Maccabi Rishon LeZion (basketball)|Maccabi Rishon LeZion]], 86–81.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Askounis |first1=Johnny |title=Deni Avdija plays last game in Europe, wins championship |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/others/1085242/deni-avdija-plays-last-game-in-europe-wins-championship/ |publisher=EuroHoops |access-date=28 July 2020 |date=28 July 2020}}</ref> He became the youngest player to ever win the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League MVP|Israeli League MVP]] award.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Lupo |first1=Nicola |title=Deni Avdija named Israeli league MVP, youngest to win award in league history |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/deni-avdija-named-israeli-league-mvp-youngest-to-win-award-in-league-history/ |publisher=Sportando |access-date=28 July 2020 |date=28 July 2020}}</ref> Avdija was also named Israeli League Israeli Player of the Year and was an [[Israeli Basketball Premier League Quintet|All-Israeli League First Team]] selection.<ref>{{cite web |title=Deni Avdija named Winner League's Israeli Player of the Year |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/others/1084675/deni-avdija-named-winner-leagues-israeli-player-of-the-year/ |publisher=EuroHoops |access-date=28 July 2020 |date=26 July 2020}}</ref> He finished the season averaging 12.9 points, 6.3 rebounds, and 2.7 assists per game in the Israeli Basketball Premier League. In the EuroLeague, Avdija averaged four points, 2.6 rebounds, and 1.2 assists in 14.3 minutes per game.<ref name="realgm">{{cite web |title=Deni Avdija Player Profile |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Deni-Avdija/Summary/116938 |publisher=[[RealGM]] |access-date=9 August 2020}}</ref>

===Washington Wizards (2020–2024)===
[[File:All-Pro Reels - 51636052177 (cropped).jpg|thumb|right|Avdija attempts a midrange shot in October 2021.]]

Avdija was selected with the ninth overall pick in the [[2020 NBA draft]] by the [[Washington Wizards]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Wizards select Deni Avdija No. 9 overall in the 2020 NBA Draft |url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/deni-avdija-pick-no-9-2020-nba-draft |website=NBA.com |access-date=19 November 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=NBA Draft 2020: Five things to know about Deni Avdija, drafted 9th overall by the Wizards |url=https://eu.usatoday.com/story/sports/2020/11/18/nba-draft-2020-deni-avdija-washington-wizards-5-facts/6339296002/ |website=eu.usatoday.com |access-date=19 November 2020}}</ref> He was projected as a consensus top 5 pick on draft night but slipped.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Braziller|first=Zach|date=2020-11-19|title=Deni Avdija falls in 2020 NBA Draft but still makes Israeli history|url=https://nypost.com/2020/11/19/deni-avdija-falls-in-2020-nba-draft-but-still-makes-israeli-history/|access-date=2021-07-10|website=New York Post}}</ref> He signed a rookie contract with the Wizards on 1 December 2020.<ref>{{cite web|title=OFFICIALLY SIGNED!|url=https://twitter.com/WashWizards/status/1333886000695808001|work=Washington Wizards twitter account|date=1 December 2020|access-date=1 December 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Wizards' Deni Avdija: Fired up and excited to play in world's best league |url=https://www.jpost.com/israel-news/sports/wizards-deni-avdija-fired-up-and-excited-to-play-in-worlds-best-league-651015 |website=jpost.com |access-date=3 December 2020}}</ref>

On 9 January 2021, Avdija recorded a then-career-high 20 points and five three-pointers, along with five rebounds, five assists, and two steals in a 128–124 loss to the [[Miami Heat]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.jpost.com/israel-news/sports/israeli-nba-phenom-deni-avdija-posts-career-high-night-vs-miami-heat-654903|first=Zachary|last=Keyser|work=[[The Jerusalem Post]]|title=Israeli NBA phenom Deni Avdija posts career-high night vs. Miami Heat|date=10 January 2021}}</ref> On 21 April, Avdija suffered a season-ending right ankle fracture during a 118–114 win against the [[Golden State Warriors]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Owens |first1=Jason |title=Wizards rookie Deni Avdija reportedly suffers broken ankle on gruesome fall |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/wizards-rookie-deni-avdija-suffers-gruesome-ankle-injury-needs-wheelchair-to-leave-court-004240341.html |website=sports.yahoo.com |access-date=21 April 2021 |date=21 April 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Curry finally goes cold, Beal rallies Wizards past Warriors |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401307682 |website=ESPN.com |access-date=22 April 2021 |date=21 April 2021}}</ref>

On 14 February 2022, Avdija set a then career high in rebounds with 15 in a 103–94 loss to the [[Detroit Pistons]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Kuzma scores 23, Wizards deal Pistons 8th straight loss |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401360677 |website=ESPN |access-date=6 November 2022 |date=14 February 2022}}</ref> During the 2021–22 season, Avdija played all 82 games while averaging 8.4 points, 5.2 rebounds, and 2.0 assists per game.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Deni Avdija 2021-22 Game Log |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/a/avdijde01/gamelog/2022/ |access-date=2022-05-01 |website=Basketball-Reference.com}}</ref>

On 11 January 2023, Avdija set a new career high in rebounds with 20 in a 100–97 win against the [[Chicago Bulls]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/news/recap-41-point-third-quarter-kuzmas-late-game-heroics-push-wizards-past-bulls-100-97|title=Recap: 41-point third quarter, Kuzma's late-game heroics push Wizards past Bulls 100-97|website=NBA.com|last=Askew|first=Luke|date=11 January 2023|access-date=11 January 2023}}</ref> On 30 January 2023, Avdija set a then career high in points with 25 in a 127–109 win against the [[San Antonio Spurs]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Wizards' Deni Avdija: Tallies game-high 25 points |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/wizards-deni-avdija-tallies-game-high-25-points/amp/ |website=[[CBSSports.com]] |date=2023-01-31 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230201174458/https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/wizards-deni-avdija-tallies-game-high-25-points/amp/ |archive-date=2023-02-01 |url-status=live}}</ref>

On 22 October 2023, Avdija and the [[Washington Wizards]] agreed to a 4-year, $55 million contract extension.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-10-22 |title=Wizards' Avdija agrees to 4-year, $55M extension |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/38720114/wizards-deni-avdija-agrees-4-year-55-million-extension |access-date=2024-08-25 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref>

On 14 February 2024, Avdija posted a new career high in points with 43, along with 15 rebounds, in a 133–126 loss to the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].<ref>{{cite web|url= https://clutchpoints.com/wizards-news-deni-avdija-gives-reason-to-hope-for-washingtons-future-with-insane-statistical-feat|title= Wizards' Deni Avdija gives fans hope for future with insane statistical feat|website=ClutchPoints|last=Pagaduan|first=Jedd|date=14 February 2024|access-date=14 February 2024}}</ref> He finished the 2023–24 season averaging career highs across every major statistical category, posting statistical averages of 14.7 points per game, 7.2 rebounds per game, 3.8 assists per game, to go along with 51% field goal percentage, 37% three-point shooting percentage, and 3.6 free throw attempts per game.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Deni Avdija {{!}} Portland Trail Blazers |url=https://www.nba.com/stats/player/1630166 |access-date=2024-08-25 |website=www.NBA.com |language=en}}</ref>

===Portland Trail Blazers (2024–present)===

==== 2024–25 season: First year in Portland ====
On 6 July 2024, Avdija was traded to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] in exchange for [[Bub Carrington]], [[Malcolm Brogdon]], and several draft selections.<ref>{{cite web|title=TRAIL BLAZERS ACQUIRE DENI AVDIJA|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-acquire-deni-avdija|website=NBA.com|date=6 July 2024|access-date=6 July 2024}}</ref>

On 2 March 2025, Avdija recorded his first career [[triple-double]] with 30 points, 12 rebounds and 10 assists in 133–129 overtime loss to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-03-02 |title=Hunter scores 32 points and Cavs hold off Blazers 133-129 in OT for 10th straight win, 50th overall |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401705433 |access-date=2025-03-02 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref> Avdija averaged 23.4 points, 9.8 rebounds and 5.2 assists over the 13 games he played in March 2025, doing so while shooting 51.0% on [[Field goal (basketball)|field goals]], and 45.7% on [[Three-point field goal|three-point]] attempts. This was the most productive month of Avdija's career up to this point, garnering attention from multiple sources across the league. On 2 April, Avdija posted his second career triple-double with 32 points, 15 rebounds and 10 assists leading the Blazers to a 127–115 overtime win over the [[Atlanta Hawks]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-04-02 |title=Sharpe and Avdija lead the Trail Blazers to a 127-113 win over the Hawks |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401705663 |access-date=2025-04-02 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref>

==== 2025–26 season: Breakout and first All-Star selection ====
After a strong first third of the [[2025–26 NBA season|2025–26 season]], highlighted by triple-doubles against the [[Chicago Bulls]], the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]], and the [[San Antonio Spurs]], Avdija averaged 25.9 points, 7.3 rebounds, and 7.1 assists in 35.2 minutes per game, emerging as the team’s primary offensive option. On 5 January 2026, Avdija was named the NBA’s Western Conference [[2025–26 NBA season#Players of the Week|Player of the Week]] for Week 11 (29 December – 4 January), for the first time in his career, after averaging 26.8 points, 8.3 rebounds, and 9.8 assists during a 3–1 week for the Blazers.<ref>{{cite web |title=Deni Avdija, Tyrese Maxey named NBA Players of the Week |url=https://www.nba.com/news/nba-players-week-deni-avdija-tyrese-maxey |website=NBA.com |date=5 January 2026 |access-date=5 January 2026}}</ref> On 7 January, Avdija scored a season-high 41 points in a 103–102 win over the [[Houston Rockets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/nba/houston-rockets/rockets-news-tari-eason-wasnt-impressed-deni-avdija-big-night|title=Rockets’ Tari Eason wasn’t impressed by Deni Avdija’s big night at all|website=ClutchPoints|last=Edañol|first=Yasmin|date=7 January 2026|access-date=7 January 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401810382|title=Avdija has 41 points, Trail Blazers hold on to beat Rockets 103-102|website=espn.com|date=7 January 2026|access-date=7 January 2026}}</ref> On 1 February, Avdija was named to his first [[2026 NBA All-Star Game|All-Star Game]] as a Western Conference reserve, becoming the first player of Israeli descent to become an All-Star in NBA history.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2026 NBA All-Star reserves announced on NBC/Peacock |url=https://www.nba.com/news/2026-all-star-reserves |access-date=2026-02-02 |website=NBA.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/news/deni-avdija-becomes-1st-israeli-named-to-nba-all-star-game|title=Deni Avdija becomes 1st Israeli named to NBA All-Star Game|website=nba.com|last=Peterson|first=Anne|date=2 February 2026|access-date=14 February 2026}}</ref> On 14 April, Avdija recorded 41 points, 7 rebounds, and 12 assists, including a decisive three-point play late in the fourth quarter, to lead the Blazers past the [[Phoenix Suns]] 114–110 in the play-in tournament, clinching the No. 7 seed.<ref>{{cite web |title=Deni Avdjia fuels late comeback as Blazers drop Suns in Play-In to clinch No. 7 seed |url=https://www.nba.com/news/trail-blazers-suns-play-in |website=NBA.com |date=April 14, 2026 |access-date=April 15, 2026}}</ref> On 19 April, Avdija was named as one of three finalists for the [[NBA Most Improved Player]] award, alongside [[Nickeil Alexander-Walker]] and [[Jalen Duren]], and finished third in the voting.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2025-26 NBA Awards: Finalists for league accolades announced {{!}} NBA.com |url=https://www.nba.com/news/2025-2026-regular-season-awards |access-date=2026-04-20 |website=NBA |language=en}}</ref>

The Blazers would face the [[San Antonio Spurs]] during their first-round series. On 19 April, Avdija made his playoff debut, putting up 30 points, ten rebounds, and five assists in a 111–98 Game 1 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=WEMBANYAMA SCORES 35 POINTS IN PLAYOFF DEBUT AS SPURS ROLL PAST TRAIL BLAZERS 111-98 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0042500151 |access-date=1 May 2026 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> The Blazers would end up losing the series in five games, with Avdija averaging 22.2 points per game.

==National team career==
===Junior national team===
Although he had also been eligible to represent [[Serbia men's national basketball team|Serbia]] internationally, due to his father's background, Avdija chose to play for [[Israel national basketball team|Israel]] because he lived there since he was born.<ref name=zadar/> He competed for [[Israel men's national under-16 basketball team|Israel]] at the [[2017 FIBA U16 European Championship]] in [[Podgorica]]. Avdija led the tournament with 12.6 rebounds and 5.3 assists per game, to go with 15.3 points per game.<ref>{{cite news|title=Avdija in the 2017 FIBA Europe Under-16 Championship|url=http://www.fiba.basketball/europe/u16/2017/player/Deni-Avdija|publisher=[[FIBA]]|date=19 August 2017|access-date=22 July 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=2017 FIBA Europe Under-16 Championship Players Statistics |url=http://www.fiba.basketball/europe/u16/2017/playerstats |website=fiba.basketball |access-date=8 March 2019}}</ref>

[[File:Deni Avdija.jpg|thumb|left|Avdija shoots a [[free throw]] for [[Israel national under-18 basketball team|Israel]] at the [[Albert Schweitzer Tournament]] in April 2018.]]

In April 2018, Avdija averaged over 17 points and nine rebounds for [[Israel national under-18 basketball team|Israel]] at the [[Albert Schweitzer Tournament]], an under-18 competition in [[Mannheim]].<ref name="halickman">{{cite web |last1=Halickman |first1=Joshua |title=Latest Israeli hoops protégé Deni Avdija finding his wings |url=https://www.jpost.com/israel-news/latest-israeli-hoops-prot%C3%A9g%C3%A9-deni-avdija-finding-his-wings-562999 |website=[[The Jerusalem Post]] |access-date=11 April 2020 |date=20 July 2018}}</ref> In July 2018, he played at the [[2018 FIBA U20 European Championship|FIBA U20 European Championship]] in [[Chemnitz]], leading [[Israel national under-20 basketball team|Israel]] to a gold medal. Avdija averaged 12.7 points, 6.4 rebounds, 1.1 assists and 1.3 steals per game, while earning a spot on the [[2018 FIBA U20 European Championship#All-Tournament Team|all-tournament team]] with teammate [[Yovel Zoosman]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fiba.basketball/europe/u20/2018/news/israel-swingman-zoosman-snatches-up-mvp-honors|title=Israel swingman Zoosman snatches up MVP honors|publisher=[[FIBA]]|date=22 July 2018|access-date=22 July 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Avdija in the 2018 FIBA Europe Under-20 Championship|url=http://www.fiba.basketball/europe/u20/2018/player/Deni-Avdija|publisher=[[FIBA]]|date=22 July 2018|access-date=22 July 2018}}</ref> Later that month, Avdija competed at the [[2018 FIBA U18 European Championship Division B|FIBA U18 European Championship Division B]] in [[Skopje]]. Appearing tired from his previous tournament and lacking in endurance, he averaged 17.3 points, 7.4 rebounds, 3 assists and 1.4 steals per game.<ref>{{cite web |title=FIBA U18 Division B – Top Performers |url=http://www.eurohopes.com/news/6263/fiba_u18_division_b_-_top_performers |publisher=Eurohopes |access-date=11 April 2020 |date=10 December 2018}}</ref>

In July 2019, Avdija led Israel to a second straight gold medal at the [[2019 FIBA U20 European Championship|FIBA U20 European Championship]] in [[Tel Aviv]]. He averaged 18.4 points, 8.3 rebounds, 5.3 assists, 2.4 blocks, and 2.1 steals per game, earning MVP and all-tournament team accolades, as the second-youngest player at the event.<ref name="obsession">{{cite web |title=In Deni Avdija's world, basketball is a 24/7 obsession |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/europe/u20/2019/news/in-deni-avdija-s-world-basketball-is-a-24/7-obsession |publisher=[[FIBA]] |access-date=10 April 2020 |date=20 July 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Deni Avdija completes MVP tournament with strong showing |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/fiba/910377/deni-avdija-completes-mvp-tournament-with-strong-showing/ |publisher=EuroHoops |access-date=11 April 2020 |date=21 July 2019}}</ref> Avdija tallied 26 points, 11 rebounds and 5 steals against France in the semifinal, before recording 23 points, 7 assists, 5 rebounds, and 3 blocks against [[Spain national under-20 basketball team|Spain]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/fiba/909981/deni-avdija-puts-on-a-show-as-israel-moves-to-final/|title=Deni Avdija puts on a show as Israel moves to Final|publisher=EuroHoops|date=20 July 2019|access-date=21 July 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/fiba/910346/avdija-powers-israel-to-the-top-of-u20-european-championship/|title=Avdija powers Israel to the top of U20 European Championship|publisher=EuroHoops|date=21 July 2019|access-date=21 July 2019}}</ref>

===Senior national team===
On 21 February 2019, Avdija made his debut for the [[Israel national basketball team|Israeli senior national team]], in an 81–77 win over [[Germany national basketball team|Germany]], during the [[2019 FIBA Basketball World Cup qualification (Europe)|2019 FIBA World Cup qualification]] stage.<ref>{{cite web|title=Israel v Germany boxscore – FIBA Basketball World Cup 2019 European Qualifiers|url=http://www.fiba.basketball/basketballworldcup/2019/european-qualifiers/game/2102/Israel-Germany|date=21 February 2019|publisher=[[FIBA]]|access-date=21 February 2019}}</ref> On 24 February 2020, he recorded 21 points and eight rebounds in 24 minutes in an 87–63 victory over [[Romania national basketball team|Romania]] during the [[EuroBasket 2021 qualification|EuroBasket 2021 qualifiers]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Avdija shines bright as Israel complete perfect first window |url=http://www.fiba.basketball/eurobasket/2021/qualifiers/news/avdija-shines-bright-as-israel-complete-perfect-first-window |publisher=[[FIBA]] |access-date=11 April 2020 |date=24 February 2020}}</ref>

At the time, his free throw shooting was not as strong as his otherwise versatile game; in 59 games for Maccabi, he averaged 59% from the free throw line and 33% from the 3-point zone.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Friedmann |first1=Liran |title=Israeli hooper Avdija set to make NBA history in coming draft |url=https://www.ynetnews.com/culture/article/Sk3QywbcP |website=ynetnews.com |access-date=18 November 2020 |date=17 November 2020}}</ref>

At the [[EuroBasket 2022]] Avdija scored 23 points along with 15 rebounds, 2 blocks and a steal leading Israel to a 89-87 victory over [[Finland men's national basketball team|Finland]] in the opening game. He averaged 14.6 points, 8.2 rebounds, 4.6 assists, 0.8 steals and 1.2 blocks per game, but Israel was eliminated at the group stage after a 2-3 winning record.

==Personal life==
His father [[Zufer Avdija]], who is of Gorani origin, was born in [[Pristina]], [[Federal People's Republic of Yugoslavia|FPR Yugoslavia]]. A professional basketball player in Yugoslavia and Israel, Zufer spent 11 years of his playing career with [[KK Crvena zvezda|Crvena zvezda]] and was the team's [[captain (sports)|captain]] in the 1980s, before moving to the [[Israeli Premier League]] in the 1990s and playing 8 seasons for [[Israel]]i clubs [[A.S. Ramat HaSharon|Ramat HaSharon]], [[Maccabi Rishon LeZion (basketball)|Rishon LeZion]], [[Hapoel Tel Aviv B.C.|Hapoel Tel Aviv]], and Elitzur [[Bat Yam]].<ref name=Bio/><ref name=obsession/><ref name="schmitz">{{cite web |last1=Schmitz |first1=Mike |title=Deni Avdija could be a polarizing top draft prospect in 2020 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/27281239/deni-avdija-polarizing-top-draft-prospect-2020 |publisher=[[ESPN]] |access-date=10 April 2020 |date=29 July 2019}}</ref> He also represented the [[Yugoslavia national basketball team|Yugoslavian national team]] internationally, with whom he won the bronze medal at the [[1982 FIBA World Championship]].<ref name="sachs"/> Avdija's mother, Sharon Artzi, an [[Israeli Jews|Israeli Jew]] from [[kibbutz]] [[Beit Zera]], is a former [[track and field]] athlete and basketball player.<ref name=maccabi/><ref name=sachs/><ref name=schmitz/><ref name="weitzman">{{cite web |last1=Weitzman |first1=Yaron |title='We've Never Had a Talent Like Him' |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2861981-weve-never-had-a-talent-like-him |publisher=[[Bleacher Report]] |access-date=10 April 2020 |date=15 November 2019}}</ref> Avdija is Jewish, and sat out his first preseason game with the Trail Blazers in 2024 [[Observance of Yom Kippur by Jewish athletes|to observe the Jewish holiday of Yom Kippur]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Cramer |first1=Philissa |title=Israeli Deni Avdija sits out Yom Kippur NBA preseason game; Jewish BYU football player suits up |url=https://www.jta.org/2024/10/14/sports/israeli-deni-avdija-sits-out-yom-kippur-nba-game-jewish-byu-football-player-suits-up |access-date=14 October 2024 |work=[[Jewish Telegraphic Agency]] |date=2024-10-14}}</ref>

He has said he learned to speak English by playing video games, as well as by watching [[Nickelodeon]] sitcoms.<ref>{{cite web | last=Hughes | first=Chase | title=Deni Avdija Learned English From 'Call of Duty' and Nickelodeon Shows | website=NBC4 Washington | date=2020-11-19 | url=https://www.nbcwashington.com/news/sports/nbcsports/deni-avdija-learned-english-from-call-of-duty-and-nickelodeon-shows/2481407/ | access-date=2025-12-13}}</ref>

Avdija holds [[Multiple citizenship|dual citizenship]] of Israel and Serbia, the latter because his father is a citizen.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NBA star Deni Avdija is taking Israeli basketball to new heights |url=https://www.olympics.com/en/news/deni-avdija-israel-basketball-new-heights-nba |last=Binner |first=Andrew |date=2021-01-29 |website=olympics.com}}</ref><ref name=zadar>{{Cite web |title=Zadar Basketball Tournament Interview: Deni Avdija |url=https://eurospects.com/zadar-basketball-tournament-interview-deni-avdija/ |last=Wawrzyńczuk |first=Bronisław |date=2018-09-18 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241126200617/https://eurospects.com/zadar-basketball-tournament-interview-deni-avdija/ |archive-date=2024-11-26}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Maccabi Tel Aviv pens long-term deal with Deni Avdija |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/547778/maccabi-tel-aviv-pens-long-term-deal-deni-avdija/ |publisher=EuroHoops |access-date=11 April 2020 |date=5 November 2017}}</ref> When he turned 18 years old, he received a deferment from mandatory service in the [[Israel Defense Forces]] (IDF) due to his basketball career.<ref name=weitzman/> 

On 1 April 2020, while the basketball season was suspended due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], Avdija was drafted into the IDF in a non-combat role called "Exceptional Athlete" status.<ref name=halickman2>{{cite web |last1=Halickman |first1=Joshua |title=Israeli basketball phenom Deni Avdija drafted into IDF |url=https://www.jpost.com/israel-news/israeli-basketball-phenom-deni-avdija-drafted-into-idf-623217 |website=[[The Jerusalem Post]] |access-date=11 April 2020 |date=1 April 2020}}</ref> "I am happy and proud to join the IDF just like every other citizen of my age,” said Avdija. “I will do whatever is asked of me just like I do on the basketball court."<ref name=halickman2> </ref> After a series of [[Palestinian political violence|Palestinian attacks]] in Israel in early 2022, Avdija wrote the phrase "[[Am Yisrael Chai]]" in Hebrew on his shoes.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Keene |first1=Louis |title=Deni Avdija wrote "Am Yisrael Chai" on his shoes. Then he played one of his best games of the year. |url=https://forward.com/fast-forward/484828/deni-avdija-wrote-am-yisrael-chai-on-his-shoes-then-dominated/ |access-date=8 December 2023 |work=[[The Forward]] |date=2022-03-31}}</ref>

In November 2025, Avdija launched Turbo, a protein ice cream brand whose name is a nod to Avdija's own nickname.<ref>{{Cite news |last=ynet |date=2025-11-30 |title=Success on and off the court: Deni 'Turbo' Avdija is launching his own ice cream brand |url=https://www.ynetnews.com/sport/article/hkueqot11wl |access-date=2026-01-12 |work=Ynetglobal |language=en}}</ref> Amidst a wider scrutiny of Israeli public figures stemming from the [[Gaza war]], in January 2026, Avdija said he was frustrated by the politicisation of his career and expressed a desire to be recognised as a basketball player rather than for his political stances.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |date=2026-02-03 |title=Meet Deni Avdija, the NBA All-Star with IDF ties congratulated by Netanyahu |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-02-03/deni-avdija-explainer-benjamin-netanyahu-nba-all-star/106299002 |access-date=2026-02-03 |work=ABC News |language=en-AU}}</ref> Following his All-Star selection, Israeli Prime Minister [[Benjamin Netanyahu]] publicly congratulated him; this drew further scrutiny of Avdija's past military service.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-02-03 |title=N12 - ההסתה נגד דני אבדיה - בעקבות הברכה של בנימין נתניהו על... |url=https://www.mako.co.il/news-sport/basketball-2026_q1/Article-09223044ae22c91026.htm |access-date=2026-02-03 |website=N12}}</ref>
